page: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3686 GB of local disk space, and the server is Premium Storage capable. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 129,546.26 and a PassMark CPU encryption test score of 102,892.71, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory performance is also strong, with a PassMark memory score in the top 10% and a small-block read-only memory bandwidth of 6,081.25 GB/sec. However, large-block read and write memory bandwidths fall into the average tier at 124.52 GB/sec and 63.74 GB/sec, respectively. The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, achieving 92.17 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 26,176.82.

The E96ads_v5 offers high resource density and cost efficiency for memory-intensive and multi-threaded workloads due to its large RAM capacity and high core count. A notable tradeoff is the lack of AVX-512 instruction support, which limits its efficiency in specific vector-heavy compute workloads, although it maintains strong performance in standard integer and cryptographic operations. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and multi-threaded software compilation.
description: The Microsoft Azure E96ads_v5 is a high-capacity, memory-optimized server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 3.525 GHz, paired with 672.0 GB of RAM and 3686 GB of local storage. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-core CPU performance and memory scores, alongside strong database capabilities, including 92.17 million Redis SET operations per second. While it lacks AVX-512 support, its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and local storage capacity make it highly cost-efficient for resource-dense deployments. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory data stores, and heavy multi-threaded enterprise workloads.
